description: The Humanitarian Data Exchange is an open platform run by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs' Centre for Humanitarian Data for sharing data across crises and organisations. On 26 September 2026 its CKAN API reported about 28,000 datasets from over 400 organisations, organised in data grids with subcategories such as food security, nutrition and poverty, geography and infrastructure, and climate hazards. Datasets are uploaded by the contributing organisations, and the related Humanitarian Exchange Language (HXL) standard tags columns for reuse. The HDX Humanitarian API (HDX HAPI), in beta, serves standardised indicators for countries with humanitarian response plans, including a rainfall hazard endpoint added in 2025. Data are accessible online at no cost through the web portal, the CKAN API and HDX HAPI, under licences chosen by each contributor, such as CC BY, CC BY-IGO, ODbL or public domain. Coverage is global, focused on crisis-affected countries. Caveats: quality, currency and licences vary by dataset, and some datasets are available only on request. It supports hazard exposure, social vulnerability and emergency response analysis for infrastructure and services in humanitarian settings; related records are healthsites.io, EM-DAT and DesInventar.
